newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: U.S. Halliburton, British Cairn Energy sign deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Halliburton, British Cairn Energy sign deal.

text.p: British Cairn Energy Plc and American Halliburton Co on Saturday signed a $235 million investment deal on gas development in Bangladesh, government officials said.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, visiting British Prime Minister John Major and Halliburton chief former U.S. defence secretary Dick Cheney witnessed the signing of the contract.
Cairn will invest $150 million to jointly develop the Sangu gas field in the Bay of Bengal with Halliburton spending $85 million.
The first gas is due to come on stream in 1998.
A U.S embassy statement on Saturday said the aim of the agreement was to develop the gas field and to bring gas by pipeline to southern Chittagong.
It said the American Occidental Corp has also recently agreed to invest $100 million for onshore gas development.
"The projects will increase U.S. investment to more than $200 million, ten times its earlier level," the statement quoted U.S. Ambassador David Merrill as saying.
Merrill said the gas that the two U.S. firms would make available would be used for producing fertiliser and electrcity.
